name: Rwanda
note: Researched 2026-06-18. Both ledgers present: Tutsi as victims of the 1994 genocide; the RPF / post-genocide state as perpetrator in reprisal killings inside Rwanda and the mass killing of Hutu refugees in Zaire/Congo (1996–97). Tolls for both events are contested and span an order of magnitude depending on methodology and political vantage; low and high ends are separately sourced.

events.title: The 1994 genocide against the Tutsi
events.tier_reasoning: Hutu Power leaders set out to eliminate the Tutsi as a group, organizing lists, roadblocks, radio incitement, and militia distribution of weapons — destruction of a group as such, the defining mark of extermination.
events.agent: Hutu Power state, the interahamwe militia, army, and ordinary Hutu civilians

toll.note: Human Rights Watch (Des Forges) put it at 'at least half a million' (~77% of a ~657,000 pre-genocide Tutsi population); a 2020 Journal of Genocide Research symposium clusters scholarly estimates at 500,000–600,000 Tutsi. The Rwandan government's official figure is 1,074,017 (it also counts moderate Hutu and Twa victims); demographers consider the 1-million-plus figure to overstate the pre-genocide Tutsi population. Davenport & Stam's low-end ~200,000-Tutsi figure is disputed and not used here as the floor.

events.summary: Over roughly a hundred days, Hutu Power leaders organized the killing of Tutsi and moderate Hutu — drawing up lists, manning roadblocks, broadcasting incitement over RTLM radio, and handing machetes to neighbours who killed neighbours.
events.relevance: Rwanda's place in the victim ledger — but the killers were also Rwandan, the cleanest case that 'victim nation' and 'perpetrator nation' can be one and the same. Audit 2026-06-18: Des Forges HRW source verified live (page states 'at least half a million ... about three quarters of the Tutsi population' and 507,000 Tutsi at ~77%); McDoom/JGR 'Contested Counting' symposium verified (McDoom's own narrow estimate 491,000–522,000, symposium cluster 500,000–600,000, ~two-thirds); government 1,074,017 verified as a real July-2000 census figure with a verified demographic over-count critique. toll.low and toll.high separately sourced.

sources.cite: Alison Des Forges, Leave None to Tell the Story: Genocide in Rwanda (Human Rights Watch, 1999) — 'at least half a million' killed, ~77% of the Tutsi population
Journal of Genocide Research symposium 'Contested Counting' (2020), incl. O. S. McDoom — scholarly consensus ~500,000–600,000 Tutsi (about two-thirds of the Tutsi population)
Government of Rwanda official count, 1,074,017 victims (cited via Rwandan genocide overview); demographers regard >1 million as an overestimate of the pre-genocide Tutsi population
sources.caveat: State figure; the post-genocide RPF government is a party with an interest in a maximal toll and a contested census baseline.

sources.cite: Philip Gourevitch, We Wish to Inform You That Tomorrow We Will Be Killed with Our Families (1998) — narrative account of the genocide's organization

events.title: RPF reprisal killings and the hunt for Hutu refugees in Congo
events.tier_reasoning: Documented as systematic killing of unarmed civilians and refugees by the RPA/AFDL during and after armed conflict; the UN Mapping Report itself notes a court might or might not find genocidal intent, so this is classed as war-crimes / crimes-against-humanity scale rather than EXT.
events.agent: The Rwandan Patriotic Front/Army (RPF/RPA) and its allied Congolese AFDL forces

toll.display: tens of thousands in Rwanda (1994); up to ~200,000+ Hutu in Congo (1996–97)
toll.note: Two linked episodes. Inside Rwanda, the suppressed 1994 Gersony Report put RPF killings at 25,000–45,000 (April–August 1994); ex-RPF minister Seth Sendashonga estimated ~60,000 through 1995. In eastern Zaire/Congo (1996–97), the UN Mapping Report described 'apparently relentless pursuit and mass killing of Hutu refugees' totalling 'several tens of thousands'; the acting UN High Commissioner (July 1997) said ~200,000 could have been massacred, and Lemarchand cites 200,000–233,000. The low (25,000) reflects the in-Rwanda floor; the high (233,000) the upper Congo estimate. Figures are heavily politically contested and the underlying counts are weak.

events.summary: As it won the 1994 war the RPF shot Hutu civilians in reprisal — findings the UN buried in the Gersony Report — and in 1996–97 Rwandan troops and their Congolese allies pursued and killed Hutu refugees across Zaire, from camps near Kisangani deep into the forest.
events.relevance: Yesterday's victims became armed actors whose killing of Hutu civilians the Rwandan state denies and criminalizes naming — proof that the lens rotates and that survivors of atrocity can author it. Audit 2026-06-18: Gersony Report verified (RPF 25,000–45,000, April–August 1994, UN-suppressed, validity disputed) — toll.low; UN Mapping Report 2010 verified ('apparently relentless pursuit and mass killing of Hutu refugees', 'several tens of thousands', genocidal intent left as an open question for a competent court, repatriations noted as a countervailing factor) — supports summary and the WAR (not EXT) tier; Lemarchand, Forgotten Genocides (2011) and the acting UN High Commissioner (8 July 1997, ~200,000) verified — toll.high 233,000. Denial-lens source: the cited Rwandan-genocide-denial page supports the 'genocide ideology'/'divisionism' laws framing generally; the specific Victoire Ingabire example (2010 Gisozi speech calling for prosecution of RPF crimes; charged under the 2008 genocide-ideology law) was corroborated independently via HRW/Amnesty and is accurate. toll.low and toll.high separately sourced; underlying Congo counts are genuinely soft (flagged in toll.note).

sources.cite: Robert Gersony / UNHCR field assessment ('Gersony Report', 1994) — RPF killed an estimated 25,000–45,000 persons, April–August 1994; suppressed by the UN
sources.caveat: Never formally published; reconstructed from leaked memos and field notes — a documented but never officially finalized assessment.

sources.cite: UN Mapping Report (OHCHR, 2010) — 'apparently relentless pursuit and mass killing of Hutu refugees', 'several tens of thousands' killed; raises but does not settle the question of genocide
René Lemarchand, Forgotten Genocides (2011), and the acting UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (8 July 1997) — ~200,000–233,000 Hutu refugees killed in Zaire/Congo, 1996–97
Reporting on Rwanda's 'genocide ideology'/'divisionism' laws used against critics (e.g. Victoire Ingabire) who call for prosecuting RPF war crimes — basis for the 'denied' lens
sources.caveat: Frames the political context of denial; not a toll source. Audit note: the cited page covers the laws/denial framing generally and does not name Ingabire; the Ingabire example is corroborated independently (HRW/Amnesty) and is accurate.
